prompt: A quantity increases from $40$ to $50$. What is the percent increase?
hint: Percent change is the change divided by the *original* value.

hints.text: Percent change is the change divided by the *original* value.
The change is $10$, and the original is $40$.

learningObjective: Compute a percent increase from two values.
explanation: Dividing by the new value instead gives $20\%$ — the standard trap on this question type.

alternativeExplanations.title: Percent change is not symmetric
steps: Going $40 \to 50$ is a $25\%$ increase, but going $50 \to 40$ is only a $20\%$ decrease.
The same absolute change of $10$ gives different percentages because the base differs.
Whenever a question walks a value up and then back down, expect this asymmetry to be the point.
